elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: The inserted paragraph says only "HDI shall indemnify the Company"; there is no "defend" (or "hold harmless") obligation and no reference to affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Indemnity runs to "the Company" only; affiliates are not named, and coverage is confined to IP claims rather than third-party claims generally.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: "any third-party claim alleging that the Site or the services provided by HDI under this Agreement infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: No limb covering HDI's breach of applicable law appears in the inserted language.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No limb covering unauthorised access to or disclosure of Company data caused by HDI.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: No gross negligence or wilful misconduct limb in the inserted paragraph.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: The insertion contains no notice mechanic; nothing elsewhere in Section 9 supplies one.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: No allocation of control of defence or settlement rights is stated.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: No cooperation obligation appears in the inserted text.

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the Agreement contains no Company (Customer) indemnity to narrow — only the Section 7.2 advertising-content covenant — and the redline does not create one, so no over-broad Customer indemnity exists.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: "HDI shall indemnify the Company against any third-party claim alleging that the Site or the services provided by HDI under this Agreement infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right".

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: "except to the extent the claim arises from modifications made by the Company" — a permitted customary exclusion.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: "combination of the Site with items not supplied by HDI" — permitted combination exclusion.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: "or the Company's specifications" — permitted specification exclusion.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: "HDI shall procure for the Company the right to continue using the affected item, or modify or replace it so that it is non-infringing".

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: "if none of those remedies is reasonably available, HDI shall refund the fees paid by the Company for the affected item".

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: "shall not exceed three (3) times the fees paid or payable by the Company under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim" — 3x a twelve-month fee base; note the cap sentence points to "this Section 9(c)", a designation that does not appear on the inserted paragraph as rendered.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Duplicate check: IP limb present as quoted above, but preferred level still fails on defend, affiliates, the non-IP limbs and the claims procedure.

reasons: All seven fallback elements are met in operative language: HDI IP indemnity for the Site and HDI's services, the modification/combination/specification exclusions, procure-modify-replace with a fee refund fallback, and a 3x twelve-month-fee super-cap. The fallback checklist is position-complete.

Preferred level is not reached: no express duty to defend, no affiliates, no limbs for breach of law, Vendor-caused data breach, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct, and no notice/control/cooperation procedure. That is acceptable because the redline is pitched at the fallback.

Minimality is satisfied: Sections 9(a) and 9(b) are retained verbatim, nothing outside the indemnity is touched, and the insertion carries no survival tail, attorneys'-fees add-on, at-own-expense language or other extras; the 3x threshold is not exceeded.

Intent defect to repair: the inserted paragraph is rendered without a subsection designation while 9(a) and 9(b) are lettered, yet its final sentence caps liability "under this Section 9(c)". As rendered this is a dangling cross-reference to a subsection that does not exist. Add the "(c)" label at the start of the inserted paragraph (or change the internal reference to "this Section 9") so the cap has a defined scope.

Optional non-blocking improvements for the margin note only: "defend" alongside "indemnify", extension to the Company's affiliates, and a notice/control/cooperation mechanic would move the clause to our preferred position.
